newsitem.title: GEORGIA: IMF tells Georgia to improve tax collection.
newsitem.headline: IMF tells Georgia to improve tax collection.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund urged the former Soviet republic of Georgia to improve tax collection and reform tax legislation.
"Georgia is in the last place among members of the Commonwealth of Independent States as far as tax revenues are concerned," IMF representative Jian-Ye Wang told Reuters late on Wednesday.

Many former Soviet republics, including Russia, are struggling to collect budgeted taxes because of widespread tax evasion and a general failure to pay bills. This, in turn, forces them to slash spending to stick to budget deficit goals.
Wang was speaking during a visit by an IMF delegation familiarising itself with conditions in Georgia.
The head of the mission, Bernd Esdar, told a news conference Georgia had notched up some economic policy successes, including stabilising the new currency, the lari, and reducing inflation.
Another IMF mission will visit Georgia in late November or early December to help officials work on the 1997 budget.
